basics.name: Model repository collections (Printables, Thingiverse, MakerWorld, GrabCAD): tags, searches and collections of print-in-place, compliant, snap-fit and mechanism models and test prints
basics.url: Printables: https://www.printables.com (the site answered with a bot-check page, HTTP 403, in this environment; its data was read through the public GraphQL API at https://api.printables.com/graphql/). Thingiverse: https://www.thingiverse.com, e.g. tag page https://www.thingiverse.com/tag/print_in_place and https://www.thingiverse.com/tag/compliant_mechanism (opened, but the content loads by JavaScript). MakerWorld: https://makerworld.com (HTTP 403 here, not verified [uncertain]). GrabCAD Community Library: https://grabcad.com/library (opened; JavaScript page)
basics.resource_type: model library (four large user-upload 3D model sharing sites; not curated encyclopedias)
basics.cost: Free to browse. Downloading is free, but GrabCAD and (by most reports) MakerWorld need a free account to download [uncertain for MakerWorld]. Printables has optional paid creator 'Clubs' and MakerWorld has a points/rewards system and paid exclusive-licence memberships; Thingiverse is free with ads
basics.license: Set per model by each uploader, so it varies model by model. Printables offers 22 licence choices (from its API): CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA, CC BY-ND, CC BY-NC, CC BY-NC-SA, CC BY-NC-ND, GPL 2.0, GPL 3.0, LGPL, BSD, 'Standard Digital File' (personal printing only, no sharing or selling), 'Commercial Use', 'Commercial Use - No Derivative', several Open Community License (OCL) variants and CERN-OHL-S v2. Thingiverse: each 'thing' carries a licence field (the API example shows 'Creative Commons - Public Domain Dedication'); mostly Creative Commons and open-source licences [uncertain on the full list]. MakerWorld: Creative Commons options plus its own 'Standard Digital File License' (personal printing only) and a 'MakerWorld Exclusive License' [uncertain, from forum posts and search snippets, since makerworld.com could not be opened]. GrabCAD: models are for private use only; non-commercial public use needs credit and a link to the original, and commercial use needs the designer's explicit permission. For the encyclopedia: linking to model pages is always fine; copying their photos or files needs the specific model's licence (many are NC or personal-use only)
basics.language: Mainly English; interfaces also in other languages (Printables tags include German and Czech words such as 'Wellengetriebe' and 'mechanismus'; MakerWorld and Printables have multi-language interfaces) [uncertain on exact language list]
basics.year: Thingiverse: launched 2008 by MakerBot, owned by Stratasys from 2013, later UltiMaker, bought by MyMiniFactory on 12 Feb 2026. Printables (Prusa Research): 2019 as PrusaPrinters, later renamed Printables [uncertain on the rename year, secondary sources say 2019 and 2022]. MakerWorld (Bambu Lab): launched September 2023. GrabCAD: community library founded around 2009-2010, now owned by Stratasys [uncertain]. All four were live and updated daily in September 2026
basics.access_barrier: none to browse Printables and Thingiverse; free login to download on GrabCAD (help page: 'When you become a GrabCAD member...') and probably MakerWorld [uncertain]. All four sites need JavaScript and some show bot-checks to scripts
basics.image_license: Photos and renders are uploaded by each designer and follow that model's licence (or none is stated); there is no site-wide open licence for images. Treat images as not reusable unless the individual model is CC-licensed, and then credit the designer
basics.authority_level: community or unvetted (user uploads; Printables and MakerWorld run contests and staff picks, and GrabCAD is used by engineers, but there is no technical review)

coverage.covers: Everything people 3D print, including a large long tail of working examples of in-scope connection and mechanism types. Printables keyword search counts (api, 2026-09-25; relevance matches, so approximate): print in place about 4,730; hinge about 4,980; ratchet about 1,400; dovetail about 1,140; gearbox about 870; snap fit about 730; bistable about 550; compliant about 480 (compliant mechanism 87); ball joint about 430; planetary gear about 390; heat set insert about 390; bayonet about 300; tolerance test about 260; differential about 210; detent about 180; magnetic latch about 180; solenoid about 135; flexure about 110; cycloidal about 90; worm gear about 76; clearance test 62; Geneva 61; universal joint 60; electromagnet 35; living hinge 33; harmonic drive 24; slip clutch 14; cam cleat 13; strain wave 11; torque limiter 2. Thingiverse has tag pages for the same ideas (e.g. print_in_place, compliant_mechanism). MakerWorld is similar and adds OpenSCAD/Fusion customisable models. GrabCAD holds engineering CAD (native and STEP files) of gearboxes, linkages, couplings, latches and so on, often not made for printing
coverage.organisation: By broad use category (Printables has 89 categories and sub-categories such as Mechanical Parts, Test Models, Engineering, Puzzles & Brain-teasers, RC & Robotics), plus free-text search and user-made tags (Printables tags are squashed words like printinplace, compliantmechanism, snapfit, tolerancetest; Thingiverse tags use underscores like print_in_place), user collections, likes/downloads/'makes' sorting and filters (Printables: printer, material, licence and more [uncertain on the full filter list]). Nothing is organised by mechanism type or behaviour. Works well if you already know the right word or can describe the object ('bag clip', 'fidget'), badly if you don't
coverage.scope_match: medium. Not a catalogue of types, but it is the biggest source of real, printable examples of almost every in-scope type (print-in-place joints, compliant and bistable mechanisms, snap fits, bayonet locks, cam cleats, ratchets, Geneva drives, cycloidal and strain-wave gearboxes, slip clutches, tolerance test prints), which is exactly what the 3D-printing-first audience needs to link to. Quality and naming are uneven
coverage.taxonomy_used: No mechanism taxonomy. Printables uses a two-level category tree (about 17 top-level groups such as 3D Printers, Art & Design, Costumes & Accessories, Fashion, Gadgets, Healthcare, Hobby & Makers, Household, Learning, Seasonal designs, Sports & Outdoor, Tabletop Miniatures, Toys & Games, World & Scans; 89 entries in total) plus free tags. Thingiverse and MakerWorld use similar use-based categories plus tags [uncertain on their exact trees]. GrabCAD uses software/format filters, categories and tags [uncertain]
coverage.example_types: Print-in-place hinge; Print-in-place cam bag clip; Print-in-place planetary gear set; Compliant mechanism (flexure) launcher; Bistable compliant mechanism (snap-through switch or pen); Compliant robot gripper; Living hinge box; Snap-fit hinge and snap-fit case; Bayonet lock (twist-lock) container; Cam cleat; Ratchet mechanism (ratchet wrench, ratchet tube squeezer); Slip clutch (spool holder with slip clutch); Torque-limiting driver; Geneva drive (Geneva mechanism fidget and clock); Cycloidal drive (cycloidal gearbox and compound cycloidal reducer); Strain-wave gear (harmonic drive); Herringbone planetary gear; Worm gear; Differential; Universal joint; Detent mechanism; Magnetic latch; Solenoid and electromagnet mounts; Tolerance and clearance test prints
coverage.making_methods: 3D printing first (FDM and resin; Printables, Thingiverse and MakerWorld); Thingiverse also hosts laser-cut and CNC files; GrabCAD is general engineering CAD (machining, sheet metal, robotics) with 3D printing as one use
coverage.item_count: Thingiverse: over 2 million to over 6 million designs depending on the source (a 2026 press summary says 6 million-plus [uncertain]; a 2026 blog says more than 2 million). Printables: about 900,000 in a 2023 community count [uncertain, now larger]; the API caps search totals at 10,000 so it cannot give the real total. MakerWorld: about 600,000 in 2023 and growing fastest [uncertain]. GrabCAD: over 5 million free CAD files and about 7 million members according to a 2026 comparison blog [uncertain]. In-scope subsets are in the low thousands (see covers)
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: torque-limiting: yes but few (Printables finds only 2 'torque limiter' and 14 'slip clutch' models); self-locking: yes, scattered (worm gears, cam cleats, locking latches), not labelled as a behaviour; hand-release only: partly (cam cleats, quick-release clips) [uncertain on how many]; one-way/ratchet: yes, many (about 1,400 'ratchet' results, ratchet wrenches, ratcheting fidgets); indexing/detent: yes (about 180 'detent' results, Geneva drives); over-centre: some (latches, bistable mechanisms) [uncertain]; compliant: yes, strong (compliant, bistable, flexure, living hinge tags); print-in-place: yes, very strong (about 4,700 results, dozens of printinplace... tags); gear trains/gearboxes: yes, strong (planetary, cycloidal, strain-wave, worm, differential, herringbone); powered connectors: some (solenoid, electromagnet and magnetic latch models, motor mounts), mostly housings rather than explanations; adhesive types: no (only occasional glue jigs; no adhesive chemistry guidance)
coverage.entry_structure: A model page with a title, photos or renders (often of real prints), a free-text description written by the designer (sometimes with print settings, clearances and assembly steps), downloadable files, tags, category, licence, likes/downloads, user 'makes' (photos of other people's prints), comments and remixes. MakerWorld and Printables often include ready-to-print 3MF profiles; GrabCAD pages show CAD files by software and a 3D viewer [uncertain]. No degrees of freedom, no standard design rules
coverage.audience_level: hobbyist (Printables, Thingiverse, MakerWorld); professional and student engineers (GrabCAD)

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: medium. Very visual (photos of real printed parts, videos on many pages, 'makes' from other users) and in everyday language, so beginners can see what a mechanism looks like and just print it. But there are no explanations of how or why a type works, names are inconsistent, and you have to know what to search for; quality varies a lot
usefulness.has_images: yes, on almost every model: photos of real prints and renders, of mixed quality (from excellent to a single blurry snapshot); interactive 3D viewers on Printables, Thingiverse and GrabCAD [uncertain for each]
usefulness.has_animations: partly: many designers embed YouTube videos or GIFs showing the mechanism moving (common for print-in-place and compliant models); interactive 3D model viewers; no simulated motion [uncertain on how common videos are]
usefulness.gaps: No type-based organisation or behaviour filters; no explanation of principles or design rules beyond what each designer writes; inconsistent naming and tag spelling (compliantmechanim, printinplaces); many untested or poor-quality models and a growing share of AI-generated models (a reason given for the 2026 Thingiverse sale); licences often non-commercial or personal-only, so images cannot be reused; pages can disappear when designers delete them; sites block scripts; almost nothing on adhesives
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: yes, per model: each model has its own permanent-looking page with an ID (Printables model pages are numbered IDs plus a slug, Thingiverse uses thing:<id>), and tag pages give a live list, e.g. https://www.thingiverse.com/tag/print_in_place or https://www.thingiverse.com/tag/compliant_mechanism. Best used as 'print one to try' links from an entry (e.g. a Geneva drive fidget, a cycloidal gearbox, a clearance tolerance test). Links can break when uploaders remove models, so prefer popular, long-lived models or tag/search pages
usefulness.reusable_data: structured, partly: Printables has a public GraphQL API (no key needed for simple read queries, but introspection is disabled and it is undocumented) giving model names, tags, categories and licences; Thingiverse has an official REST API with Swagger docs that needs a registered app token (Openverse uses it and keeps only CC0 models); GrabCAD and MakerWorld are scrape-only [uncertain on any MakerWorld API]. There is no licence for the lists themselves; each model's own licence applies to its files and images, and the sites' terms of use restrict scraping [uncertain]
usefulness.maintained: yes, all four are active in 2026. Thingiverse was bought by MyMiniFactory on 12 Feb 2026 and stays a separate site; Printables and MakerWorld are actively developed by printer makers (Prusa Research, Bambu Lab); GrabCAD is run by Stratasys (help page last updated October 2020 but the site footer says 2026). Individual models come and go
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) Link each encyclopedia entry to a curated 'try it' model, preferably a print-in-place or fidget demo, plus a clearance/tolerance test print, so beginners can hold the mechanism. (2) Show 'makes' (other people's photos of real results), which builds trust. (3) Tag vocabulary shows the words makers actually use (printinplace, snapfit, fidget, bistable, tolerancetest), useful as aliases and search terms in the flow chart. (4) Customiser buttons (Thingiverse Customizer, MakerWorld Parametric Model Maker using OpenSCAD or Fusion parameters) are a good pattern for a 'make your own size' link. (5) Printables' licence picker is a good example of labelling reuse rights clearly on each item
usefulness.design_rules_given: only informally: some designers state clearances, layer heights or tested materials in their descriptions, and there are hundreds of tolerance/clearance test prints (Printables: about 260 'tolerance test' and 62 'clearance test' results) which let users measure their own printer's fit. No systematic numbers
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: yes, partly: Thingiverse Customizer (runs OpenSCAD files with sliders; tag a thing 'customizer'); MakerWorld Parametric Model Maker (OpenSCAD, and Autodesk Fusion files since June 2025 per secondary reports [uncertain]); Printables hosts many parametric SCAD and CAD source files and has announced parametric models [uncertain]; GrabCAD offers native CAD files that can be edited
usefulness.file_formats: STL and 3MF (with print profiles on MakerWorld and Printables), OBJ, STEP, SCAD, F3D and other native CAD files (GrabCAD: SolidWorks, Fusion, Inventor, STEP, IGES and more [uncertain]), plus SVG/DXF for laser cutting on Thingiverse, photos, and embedded video links
usefulness.terminology_value: low. Tags and titles are user-chosen, often misspelled or informal ('fidget', 'clicky'), and occasionally correct engineering names (strain wave gear, cycloidal reducer, Geneva drive). Useful to learn the words beginners use, not as an authority
usefulness.decision_support: none for choosing a connection type: only search, tags, category filters, sorting by popularity, and (Printables) filters for printer/material/licence [uncertain on the exact filters]. No comparisons or flow chart
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: Many models are cross-posted on two or more of these sites (and Cults, MyMiniFactory, Thangs); aggregators like Yeggi, STLFinder and Thangs index them all. Thingiverse Customizer's format is the OpenSCAD Customizer standard also used by MakerWorld's Parametric Model Maker. Remixes chain back to originals, so cite the original designer's page. Designs often implement types described in BYU CMR, BOSL2 and 507 Mechanical Movements
